newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees low price boosting wheat imports in 97.
newsitem.headline: China sees low price boosting wheat imports in 97.

text.p: A Chinese newspaper on Thursday forecast a stable domestic wheat market in 1997 and said falling world prices would create a favourable environment for wheat imports.
International wheat prices were expected to drop in 1997, the Economic Information Daily said.
"This will have major significance in changing the unfavourable wheat import situation," the newspaper said.
The domestic wheat market would be basically stable in 1997, with supply slightly exceeding demand after a bumper harvest in 1996, it said.
Domestic prices were seen fluctuating between 1,600-1,800 yuan ($192-$217) a tonne, with a slight rise in the second half of the year, it said.

China's total purchases of domestic wheat had reached 18.53 million tonnes between January and July, 1996, with state purchases accounting for 13.12 million tonnes, it said but gave no further details.
